questions.text: Explain why the velocity of circulation is likely to decrease during a recession.
questions.expectedAnswer: During a recession, consumer confidence falls and households spend less.
questions.markingGuide: Links recession to lower consumer confidence/spending leading to higher uncertainty and less spending, therefore lower V.

questions.text: Assuming all other variables remain constant, use the quantity theory of money to explain how a decrease in the velocity of circulation will impact inflation.
questions.markingGuide: Explains a decrease in P using the equation MV=PQ, showing the proportional relationship between V and P.

questions.text:
Use the quantity theory of money and the business cycle to explain how a recession may impact overall inflation.

In your answer, include:
• why real output may decrease during a recession
• how the change in velocity of circulation as well as real output will impact the price level in the economy.
questions.expectedAnswer: In a recession, real output (Q) decreases as businesses reduce production due to lower demand...
questions.markingGuide: Fully explains the less-than-proportionate change in P: V decrease pushes P down, Q decrease pushes P up; integrates business cycle and MV=PQ.

questions.text:
Define inflation.

New Zealand's annual inflation rate in 2023 was 4.7 per cent. This is a decrease from the annual rate in 2022, when it was 7.2 per cent.
questions.expectedAnswer: Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services over time.

questions.text: Explain whether workers on the minimum wage would prefer a lower or higher inflation rate.
questions.expectedAnswer: Workers on minimum wage would prefer lower inflation.
questions.markingGuide: Explains why a lower inflation rate is preferred — real income/purchasing power maintained.

questions.text: Explain whether savers would prefer a lower or higher inflation rate.
questions.markingGuide: Identifies that a lower inflation rate is preferred and explains the impact on purchasing power of savings.

questions.text:
